title: Reasons for Merger and Alignment Plans for Yale-NUS College and other NUS Schools, and Impact on Students' Educational Experience
what_it_is: Reasons for Merger and Alignment Plans for Yale-NUS College and other NUS Schools, and Impact on Students' Educational Experience

sections.label: Questions on Yale-NUS closure
sections.summary: Questions ask the Education Minister about considerations, stakeholder consultation and public monies spent on Yale-NUS College since its inception.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what are the considerations behind the closure of Yale-NUS College and its planned merger with the University Scholars Programme (USP) into the New College; (b) how the various key stakeholders were consulted; and (c) how much public monies through the Ministry's subsidies, grants and funding have been spent on Yale-NUS College since its inception.

sections.label: Questions on merger motivations
sections.summary: Questions ask about merger motivations, financial factors, Yale's willingness, notification timing, consultation, alternatives, decision date, impact, metrics and student activism.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education regarding the decision to merge Yale-NUS College and NUS' University Scholars Programme (a) what are the motivations behind the decision; (b) whether financial factors feature in the decision; (c) whether Yale University provided any indication of willingness to continue the partnership beyond 2025; (d) why was the decision not conveyed to the student body in advance, closer to the announcement of the new College of Humanities and Sciences; and (e) whether the faculty and student body of Yale-NUS College were consulted before the decision and if not, why not.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in light of the announced merger of Yale-NUS College and NUS' University Scholars Programme to create the "New College" (a) what have been the other alternatives considered and why are these options not taken; (b) when was the decision for merger made; and (c) what is the assessment on the impact on NUS' and Singapore’s international academic standing from this decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether there are any key performance indicators for the Yale-NUS College and what was the assessed performance on those metrics; (b) what has been the past impact of the Yale-NUS College on admissions into NUS; (c) whether there are future plans for a dedicated liberal arts college; (d) what are the plans to preserve Singapore’s reputation for quality tertiary education partnerships; and (e) whether student activism at the Yale-NUS College played any part in the closure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, it is a very successful residential living and learning model that admits around 220 students each year and has produced about 2,500 alumni to date.

sections.label: YNC endowment fundraising target
sections.summary: YNC had hoped to raise over S$300 million to reach an endowment fund size of around S$1 billion, with Government matching and investment returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: YNC had hoped to raise over S$300 million to reach an endowment fund size of around S$1 billion, with Government matching and investment returns.

sections.label: NUS merger decision
sections.summary: NUS decided to build on the best features of YNC and USP by merging YNC with the USP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: NUS has decided that it is time to build on the best features of YNC and USP, and to take a step forward to expand access and enhance the scope of its educational offerings, by merging YNC with the USP.

sections.label: NUS-Yale discussions start
sections.summary: In early-July 2021, NUS initiated discussions with Yale University.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In early-July 2021, NUS initiated discussions with Yale University.

sections.label: Transition time and final intake
sections.summary: Faculty and staff had until 2025 to work through transition details, making YNC's 2021 intake its final cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This allowed faculty and staff the maximum time – between now and 2025 – to work through the details of the transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This also means that YNC’s 2021 intake would be its final cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Class of 2025 cohort would have the full four years to complete their undergraduate studies at YNC.

sections.label: Current students' degree assurance
sections.summary: NUS and YNC assured current students they will graduate with the same degree as their predecessors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: NUS and YNC have assured all current students that they will graduate with the same degree as their predecessors.

sections.label: No faculty staff redundancy
sections.summary: No faculty or staff will be made redundant as a result of the merger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For faculty and staff, no one will be made redundant as a result of this merger.

sections.label: Yale advisory role
sections.summary: Yale, a longstanding NUS friend and YNC partner, agreed to an advisory role in the New College's international advisory panel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yale has been a longstanding friend of NUS and a visionary partner in the YNC College.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We are glad that Yale has agreed to play an advisory role in the New College as a pioneering member of the College’s international advisory panel.

sections.label: New College retained elements
sections.summary: The New College will retain the best elements of both institutions, including residential component, small-group teaching, common curriculum and immersive experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The New College will retain the best elements of both institutions, including a residential component, YNC’s practice of small-group teaching, a common curriculum and an overall immersive experience.

sections.label: Scale benefits for education
sections.summary: With benefits of scale, education in the New College can be more inclusive, affordable and flexible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With the benefits of scale, education in the New College can be much more inclusive, affordable and flexible.

sections.label: MOE support and lower fees
sections.summary: MOE is committed to supporting the New College, expecting tuition fees and costs per student to be lower than at YNC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) is committed to supporting the New College.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We expect that the tuition fees and costs per student will be lower than that at YNC, in keeping with the vision for the New College to be a more inclusive, affordable and accessible model of education.

sections.label: YNC and NUS intake sizes
sections.summary: YNC takes in about 250 students a year, compared to NUS' intake of about 7,000 students a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: YNC takes in about 250 students a year compared to NUS' intake of about 7,000 students a year.

sections.label: MOE grants to YNC
sections.summary: In 2020, MOE provided around $48 million yearly to YNC for about 1,000 students, more than double NUS' per student rate for Humanities and Science.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In 2020, MOE provided around $48 million to YNC in operating grants per year for about 1,000 students in YNC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On a per student basis, this was more than double that of a Humanities and Science student in NUS on average, reflective of the higher cost in education.

sections.label: Merging YNC and USP
sections.summary: Merging YNC and USP to form the New College lets NUS combine both sides' best elements and achieve economies of scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Merging YNC and USP to form the New College therefore allows NUS to combine the best elements of both sides and to achieve economies of scale to allow us to scale this experience to many more students in part or in full across NUS.

sections.label: International student proportions
sections.summary: YNC takes in about 40% of its cohort from the international student community, while NUS takes in about 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, today, YNC takes in about 40% of its cohort from the international student community; NUS takes in about 10%.

sections.label: Combining USP and YNC
sections.summary: NUS decided combining USP and YNC best achieves inclusivity and affordability, and is building new foreign university partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second is to make sure that the whole experience in our Universities is much more inclusive, much more affordable, much more accessible to a wider number of students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is based on these that we decided that amongst the various options, whether to continue the current model, to merge the USP with YNC or to even develop a separate model as someone who would have said, that amongst all these different models, NUS has decided that the best way to achieve both objectives that I have just illustrated is to combine the USP and the YNC programme together to make it much more affordable and accessible to many more students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the Member's second supplementary question about our posture towards the international partnerships with other foreign universities, indeed, as we speak today, we are in the process of building up new partnerships with other universities across the world.

sections.label: NUS contacting students
sections.summary: NUS is in contact with students who may want to consider other options and to see how best to help them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: NUS is in contact with the students who may want to consider other options and to see how we can best render help to them.

sections.label: NUS success and global graduates
sections.summary: Speaker states NUS success means producing globally minded graduates, learning from the world while charting its own way, and reinforcing Singapore's standing through openness, integration and inclusivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, to me, in time to come, I will consider it a success if NUS produces quality graduates that are much more global in their perspective, able to connect the East and the West, the North and the South; that these students will be able to provide unique solutions in context to the challenges that Singapore faces and if possible, to make a contribution to the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, NUS will continue to be successful if NUS continues to remain humble and learn from the best in the world, while at the same time, being confident to chart out its own way forward, so that NUS is not just copying from the best in the world but instead, in the process, create something new, create something better that in and of itself becomes a valued partner to the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Third, that NUS, as a University, will help to reinforce Singapore's standing in the world because we stand for openness, integration, inclusivity.

sections.label: NUS students serving Singapore
sections.summary: Speaker says if NUS students embody success beyond themselves for country, people and future, NUS and its students would have served Singapore for generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If the NUS students can embody this spirit of being successful beyond themselves for the country, for our people and for our future, I think NUS and NUS students would have done Singapore a great service for many generations to come.
